name: Peloponnese, Greece

visa.notes: Financially independent person visa requires ~€2,000/mo income proof.

rent.notes: Asking rents May 2026: Kalamata 2BR EUR 690 / 3BR EUR 850, Nafplio 740/910, smaller Messinia/Laconia towns EUR 450-600; Expat Exchange reports EUR 500-600 for 2BR in central Kalamata. Pet-friendly 2-3BR house with yard sits around EUR 700. Spitogatos Q2 2026 index shows national rents up only 1.3% y/y.

groceries.notes: Two adults ~EUR 280-350 (expat reports USD 300-400 in Kalamata) plus EUR 100+/month food for a large-breed dog. ELSTAT Sept 2026 food and non-alcoholic beverages CPI only +0.6% y/y so food prices are essentially flat since spring.

utilities.notes: DEI green tariff Nov 2026: EUR 0.169/kWh up to 200 kWh, 0.284/kWh above, plus EUR 5 fixed and regulated network charges; ELSTAT housing/energy CPI +14.7% y/y in Sept 2026. A 2-3BR house with AC in summer and electric/oil heating in winter runs ~EUR 110-130 electricity averaged, plus water/sewer/municipal fees ~EUR 25-35. Excludes internet.

healthcare.notes: Non-EU retirees on the FIP/retirement permit must carry private cover valid in Greece (EUR 600-1,800 per person per year; at age 60 expect the upper half, ~EUR 100-150 per person per month with Interamerican/Ethniki/NN). Alternative is voluntary EOPYY enrolment at 8.5% of declared pension income (would exceed EUR 400/month on this household's income). Typical reflects two local private plans; max reflects international plans (EUR 100-500/person) which rise 12-14% a year.

insurance.notes: Re-modeled from old template (which carried health cover) to tenant contents insurance only. Greek contents policies start around EUR 35/year (Eurolife Sweet Home Content); a EUR 30-50k contents sum with liability runs roughly EUR 100-200/year. Health cover now sits fully in healthcare.

transportation.notes: One mid-size petrol car in a rural region: unleaded ~EUR 1.99/L nationally (July 2026) and transport CPI +11.3% y/y in Sept 2026, ~55-60 L/month = EUR 110-120; insurance EUR 300-600/yr; road tax EUR 135-300/yr; KTEO and maintenance ~EUR 30-40/month. KTEL buses are sparse so a car is needed; Kalamata city bus pass ~EUR 20.

healthcare.system: Regional hospitals in Patras and Kalamata. Basic care adequate; specialist care may require Athens travel (2-3 hours).
healthcare.waitTimes: Public: 4-12 weeks. Smaller towns have longer waits.

pros: Among the most affordable areas in the EU
